newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Twenty-two die in southern Philippines fighting.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-two die in southern Philippines fighting.

text.p: Philippine troops backed by helicopter gunships killed at least 20 Moslem rebels in fierce fighting on southern Mindanao island, the military said on Wednesday.

Two soldiers died and four others were wounded in fighting that erupted on Tuesday around the town of Buldon in Maguindanao province, about 800 km (500 miles) south of Manila, an official military report said.

Seven army helicopters, firing rockets and machine-guns, backed ground troops in the clashes involving hundreds of soldiers and about 400 guerrillas of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), which is fighting for an Islamic state in Mindanao and adjacent islands.
"The operating troops are conducting clearing-up operations," the report obtained by Reuters said.

The figure on rebel casualties was based on a body count, military spokesman Major Teddy Covarubias told reporters in southern Zamboanga city. Soldiers also recovered more than a dozen assault rifles from the rebels, he said.
The MILF is a breakaway faction of the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front, which concluded a peace deal with President Fidel Ramos's government in October last year.

The MILF is not a party to the deal but held separate preliminary talks with a government panel on January 7 on ending their own rebellion. Both sides had agreed to resume their talks on February 25-26.
The two sides had also reached a tentative agreement on a temporary cease-fire.
The military reinforced its forces around Buldon last week after suspected MILF rebels ambushed a convoy carrying Buldon town Mayor Macarampat Manalao on Saturday, killing two soldiers.
Southern military commander Major General Romeo Padiernos accused the MILF of violating the cease-fire and rejected a demand to withdraw his forces.
The MILF responded by accusing the army of deploying troops around Buldon in preparation for attacks on the MILF's main base in the area, Camp Abubakar, and demanded their withdrawal.
"We have not entered their territory but this was what they did," Padiernos told reporters on Tuesday.
Camp Abubakar is a heavily fortified rebel base which houses a rebel "military academy" and several Islamic schools for thousands of Moslem civilians residing in the area.
The MILF claims to have 60,000 to 80,000 fighters but the military estimates their strength at between 6,000 to 8,000.
